Because we do not apply hedge accounting for commodity derivative contracts, all realized and unrealized gains and losses from commodity derivative contracts are recognized in our consolidated statement of income.  Gains and losses from derivative contracts held for trading not directly related to our physical business are reported net in the &#x201c;Other income&#x201d; line on our consolidated statement of income.  Cash flows from all our derivative activity for the periods presented appear in the operating section on our consolidated statement of cash flows.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Purchase and sales contracts with firm minimum notional volumes for commodities that are readily convertible to cash are recorded on our consolidated balance sheet as derivatives unless the contracts are eligible for, and we elect, the normal purchases and normal sales exception, whereby the contracts are recorded on an accrual basis.  We generally apply the normal purchases and normal sales exception to eligible crude oil, refined petroleum product, NGL, natural gas and power commodity contracts to purchase or sell quantities we expect to use or sell in the normal course of business.  All other derivative instruments are recorded at fair value on our consolidated balance sheet.  For further information on the fair value of our derivatives, see &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note 13&#x2014;Fair Value Measurements&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Commodity Derivative Contracts&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;We sell into or receive supply from the worldwide crude oil, refined petroleum product, NGL, natural gas and electric power markets, exposing our revenues, purchases, cost of operating activities and cash flows to fluctuations in the prices for these commodities.  Generally, our policy is to remain exposed to the market prices of commodities; however, we use futures, forwards, swaps and options in various markets to balance physical systems, meet customer needs, manage price exposures on specific transactions, and do a limited amount of trading not directly related to our physical business, all of which may reduce our exposure to fluctuations in market prices.  We also use the market knowledge gained from these activities to capture market opportunities such as moving physical commodities to more profitable locations, storing commodities to capture seasonal or time premiums, and blending commodities to capture quality upgrades.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following table indicates the consolidated balance sheet line items that include the fair values of commodity derivative assets and liabilities. into interest rate swaps to hedge the variability of lease payments on our headquarters facility.  These monthly lease payments vary based on monthly changes in the one-month LIBOR and changes, if any, in our credit rating over the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;five&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;-year term of the lease. We have designated these swaps as cash flow hedges. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The aggregate net fair value of these swaps, which is included in the &#x201c;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#x201d; and &#x201c;Other assets&#x201d; lines on our consolidated balance sheet, totaled &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$15 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; at &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, respectively. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We report the mark-to-market gains or losses on our interest rate swaps designated as highly effective cash flow hedges as a component of other comprehensive income (loss), and reclassify such gains and losses into earnings in the same period during which the hedged transaction affects earnings.  Net realized gains and losses from settlements of the swaps were immaterial for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;three and six months&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We currently estimate that pre-tax gains of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; will be reclassified from accumulated other comprehensive loss into general and administrative expenses during the next 12 months as the hedged transactions settle; however, the actual amounts that will be reclassified will vary based on changes in interest rates.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Credit Risk from Derivative Instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The credit risk from our derivative contracts, such as forwards and swaps, derives from the counterparty to the transaction.  Individual counterparty exposure is managed within predetermined credit limits and includes the use of cash-call margins when appropriate, thereby reducing the risk of significant nonperformance.  We also use futures, swaps and option contracts that have a negligible credit risk because these trades are cleared with an exchange clearinghouse and subject to mandatory margin requirements, typically on a daily basis, until settled.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Certain of our derivative instruments contain provisions that require us to post collateral if the derivative exposure exceeds a threshold amount.  We have contracts with fixed threshold amounts and other contracts with variable threshold amounts that are contingent on our credit rating.  The variable threshold amounts typically decline for lower credit ratings, while both the variable and fixed threshold amounts typically revert to zero if our credit ratings fall below investment grade.  Cash is the primary collateral in all contracts; however, many contracts also permit us to post letters of credit as collateral.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The aggregate fair values of all derivative instruments with such credit-risk-related contingent features that were in a liability position were immaterial at &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;December&#160;31, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</psx:FinancialInstrumentsAndDerivativeContractsTextBlock>

    <us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-CB4B6BC18CB940762175D28B34D4538C-0-wk-Fact-337B9942A604BE095E0FD28B3472C14D">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;color:#000000;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Note 13&#x2014;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;color:#000000;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Fair Value Measurements&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Recurring Fair Value Measurements&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We carry certain assets and liabilities at fair value, which we measure at the reporting date using the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (i.e., an exit price), and disclose the quality of these fair values based on the valuation inputs used in these measurements under the following hierarchy:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 1: Fair value measured with unadjusted quoted prices from an active market for identical assets or liabilities.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 2: Fair value measured either with: (1) adjusted quoted prices from an active market for similar assets or liabilities; or (2) other valuation inputs that are directly or indirectly observable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 3: Fair value measured with unobservable inputs that are significant to the measurement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We classify the fair value of an asset or liability based on the significance of its observable or unobservable inputs to the measurement.  However, the fair value of an asset or liability initially reported as Level 3 will be subsequently reported as Level 2 if the unobservable inputs become inconsequential to its measurement or corroborating market data becomes available.  Conversely, an asset or liability initially reported as Level 2 will be subsequently reported as Level 3 if corroborating market data becomes unavailable.  For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;six months ended&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, derivative assets with an aggregate value of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$91 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and derivative liabilities with an aggregate value of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$51 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; were transferred to Level 1 from Level 2, as measured from the beginning of the reporting period.  The measurements were reclassified within the fair value hierarchy due to the availability of unadjusted quoted prices from an active market.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We used the following methods and assumptions to estimate the fair value of financial instruments:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Cash and cash equivalents&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Accounts and notes receivable&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Derivative instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;We fair value our exchange-traded contracts based on quoted market prices obtained from the New York Mercantile Exchange, the Intercontinental Exchange or other exchanges, and classify them as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.  When exchange-cleared contracts lack sufficient liquidity, or are valued using either adjusted exchange-provided prices or non-exchange quotes, we classify those contracts as Level 2.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Physical commodity forward purchase and sales contracts and over-the-counter (OTC) financial swaps are generally valued using forward quotes provided by brokers and price index developers, such as Platts and Oil Price Information Service. We corroborate these quotes with market data and classify the resulting fair values as Level 2.  When forward market prices are not available, we estimate fair value using the forward price of a similar commodity, adjusted for the difference in quality or location.  In certain less liquid markets or for longer-term contracts, forward prices are not as readily available.  In these circumstances, physical commodity purchase and sales contracts and OTC swaps are valued using internally developed methodologies that consider historical relationships among various commodities that result in management&#x2019;s best estimate of fair value.  We classify these contracts as Level 3.  Physical and OTC commodity options are valued using industry-standard models that consider various assumptions, including quoted forward prices for commodities, time value, volatility factors and contractual prices for the underlying instruments, as well as other relevant economic measures.  The degree to which these inputs are observable in the forward markets determines whether the options are classified as Level 2 or 3.  We use a mid-market pricing convention (the mid-point between bid and ask prices).  When appropriate, valuations are adjusted to reflect credit considerations, generally based on available market evidence.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We determine the fair value of our interest rate swaps based on observed market valuations for interest rate swaps that have notional amounts, terms and pay and reset frequencies similar to ours.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Rabbi trust assets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;These deferred compensation investments are measured at fair value using unadjusted quoted prices available from national securities exchanges and are therefore categorized as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Debt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;The carrying amount of our floating-rate debt approximates fair value.  The fair value of our fixed-rate debt is estimated based on observable market prices.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following tables display the fair value hierarchy for our financial assets and liabilities either accounted for or disclosed at fair value on a recurring basis.  These values are determined by treating each contract as the fundamental unit of account; therefore, derivative assets and liabilities with the same counterparty are shown on a gross basis in the hierarchy sections of these tables, before the effects of counterparty and collateral netting.  The following tables also reflect the effect of netting derivative assets and liabilities with the same counterparty for which we have the legal right of offset and collateral netting.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div     <us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-1EEF51F7FE421C74E011D28B34D4A50B-0-wk-Fact-40CB6F1EA0DBC1D6D8EFD28B34726026">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Recurring Fair Value Measurements&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We carry certain assets and liabilities at fair value, which we measure at the reporting date using the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (i.e., an exit price), and disclose the quality of these fair values based on the valuation inputs used in these measurements under the following hierarchy:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 1: Fair value measured with unadjusted quoted prices from an active market for identical assets or liabilities.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 2: Fair value measured either with: (1) adjusted quoted prices from an active market for similar assets or liabilities; or (2) other valuation inputs that are directly or indirectly observable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 3: Fair value measured with unobservable inputs that are significant to the measurement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We classify the fair value of an asset or liability based on the significance of its observable or unobservable inputs to the measurement.  However, the fair value of an asset or liability initially reported as Level 3 will be subsequently reported as Level 2 if the unobservable inputs become inconsequential to its measurement or corroborating market data becomes available.  Conversely, an asset or liability initially reported as Level 2 will be subsequently reported as Level 3 if corroborating market data becomes unavailable.  For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;six months ended&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, derivative assets with an aggregate value of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$91 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and derivative liabilities with an aggregate value of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$51 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; were transferred to Level 1 from Level 2, as measured from the beginning of the reporting period.  The measurements were reclassified within the fair value hierarchy due to the availability of unadjusted quoted prices from an active market.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We used the following methods and assumptions to estimate the fair value of financial instruments:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Cash and cash equivalents&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Accounts and notes receivable&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Derivative instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;We fair value our exchange-traded contracts based on quoted market prices obtained from the New York Mercantile Exchange, the Intercontinental Exchange or other exchanges, and classify them as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.  When exchange-cleared contracts lack sufficient liquidity, or are valued using either adjusted exchange-provided prices or non-exchange quotes, we classify those contracts as Level 2.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Physical commodity forward purchase and sales contracts and over-the-counter (OTC) financial swaps are generally valued using forward quotes provided by brokers and price index developers, such as Platts and Oil Price Information Service. We corroborate these quotes with market data and classify the resulting fair values as Level 2.  When forward market prices are not available, we estimate fair value using the forward price of a similar commodity, adjusted for the difference in quality or location.  In certain less liquid markets or for longer-term contracts, forward prices are not as readily available.  In these circumstances, physical commodity purchase and sales contracts and OTC swaps are valued using internally developed methodologies that consider historical relationships among various commodities that result in management&#x2019;s best estimate of fair value.  We classify these contracts as Level 3.  Physical and OTC commodity options are valued using industry-standard models that consider various assumptions, including quoted forward prices for commodities, time value, volatility factors and contractual prices for the underlying instruments, as well as other relevant economic measures.  The degree to which these inputs are observable in the forward markets determines whether the options are classified as Level 2 or 3.  We use a mid-market pricing convention (the mid-point between bid and ask prices).  When appropriate, valuations are adjusted to reflect credit considerations, generally based on available market evidence.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We determine the fair value of our interest rate swaps based on observed market valuations for interest rate swaps that have notional amounts, terms and pay and reset frequencies similar to ours.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Rabbi trust assets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;These deferred compensation investments are measured at fair value using unadjusted quoted prices available from national securities exchanges and are therefore categorized as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Debt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&#x2014;The carrying amount of our floating-rate debt approximates fair value.  The fair value of our fixed-rate debt is estimated based on observable market prices.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy>

    <us-gaap:LesseeFinanceLeasesTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-35727AE524B94F038A2ED28B34D4120A-0-wk-Fact-DF0ACB7C276A7886B5EFD28B345A38FB">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Note 14&#x2014;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We lease marine vessels, tugboats, barges, pipelines, storage tanks, railcars, service station sites, office buildings, corporate aircraft, land and other facilities and equipment.  In determining whether an agreement contains a lease, we consider our ability to control the asset and whether there are limitations on our control through third-party participation or vendor substitution rights.  Certain leases include escalation clauses for adjusting rental payments to reflect changes in price indices, as well as renewal options and/or options to purchase the leased property.  Renewal options have been included only when reasonably certain of exercise.  There are no significant restrictions imposed on us in our lease agreements with regards to dividend payments, asset dispositions or borrowing ability.  Certain leases have residual value guarantees, which may require additional payments at the end of the lease term if future fair values decline below contractual lease balances.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;In our implementation of ASU No. 2016-02, we elected to discount lease obligations using our incremental borrowing rate.  Furthermore, we elected to separate costs for lease and service components for contracts involving the following asset types: marine vessels, tugboats, barges and consignment service stations.  For these contracts, we allocate the consideration payable between the lease and service components using the relative standalone prices of each component.  For contracts involving all other asset types, we elected the practical expedient to account for the lease and service components on a combined basis.  Our right-of-way agreements in effect prior to January 1, 2019, were not accounted for as leases as they were not initially determined to be leases at their commencement dates.  However, modifications to these agreements or new agreements will be assessed and accounted for accordingly under ASU No. 2016-02.  For short-term leases, which are leases that, at the commencement date, have a lease term of 12 months or less and do not include an option to purchase the underlying asset that is reasonably certain to exercise, we elected to not recognize the ROU asset and corresponding lease liability on our consolidated balance sheet.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following table indicates the consolidated balance sheet line items that include the ROU assets and lease liabilities for our finance and operating leases: &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="padding-left:0px;text-indent:0px;line-height:normal;padding-top:10px;"&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New     <us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeasesTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2019Q2YTD"
      id="TextSelection-F4215740B7AE71378552D28B34D477F8-0-wk-Fact-D5B719C881273204E29BD28B34875B7D">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Note 14&#x2014;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Leases&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We lease marine vessels, tugboats, barges, pipelines, storage tanks, railcars, service station sites, office buildings, corporate aircraft, land and other facilities and equipment.  In determining whether an agreement contains a lease, we consider our ability to control the asset and whether there are limitations on our control through third-party participation or vendor substitution rights.  Certain leases include escalation clauses for adjusting rental payments to reflect changes in price indices, as well as renewal options and/or options to purchase the leased property.  Renewal options have been included only when reasonably certain of exercise.  There are no significant restrictions imposed on us in our lease agreements with regards to dividend payments, asset dispositions or borrowing ability.  Certain leases have residual value guarantees, which may require additional payments at the end of the lease term if future fair values decline below contractual lease balances.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;In our implementation of ASU No. 2016-02, we elected to discount lease obligations using our incremental borrowing rate.  Furthermore, we elected to separate costs for lease and service components for contracts involving the following asset types: marine vessels, tugboats, barges and consignment service stations.  For these contracts, we allocate the consideration payable between the lease and service components using the relative standalone prices of each component.  For contracts involving all other asset types, we elected the practical expedient to account for the lease and service components on a combined basis.  Our right-of-way agreements in effect prior to January 1, 2019, were not accounted for as leases as they were not initially determined to be leases at their commencement dates.  However, modifications to these agreements or new agreements will be assessed and accounted for accordingly under ASU No. 2016-02.  For short-term leases, which are leases that, at the commencement date, have a lease term of 12 months or less and do not include an option to purchase the underlying asset that is reasonably certain to exercise, we elected to not recognize the ROU asset and corresponding lease liability on our consolidated balance sheet.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following table indicates the consolidated balance sheet line items that include the ROU For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;three and six months&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, Phillips 66 Partners generated net proceeds of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$58 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$67 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, respectively, under its ATM programs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Phillips 66 Partners holds an investment in the Gray Oak Pipeline through Holdings LLC.  In December 2018, a third party exercised its option to acquire a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;35%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; interest in Holdings LLC.  Because Holdings LLC&#x2019;s sole asset was its ownership interest in Gray Oak, which is considered a financial asset, and because certain restrictions were placed on the third party&#x2019;s ability to transfer or sell its interest in Holdings LLC during the construction of the Gray Oak Pipeline, the legal sale of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;35%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; interest did not qualify as a sale under GAAP.  As such, the contributions the third party is making to Holdings LLC to cover its share of previously incurred and future construction costs plus a premium to Phillips 66 Partners are reflected as a long-term obligation in the &#x201c;Other liabilities and deferred credits&#x201d; line on our consolidated &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;balance sheet and financing cash inflows in the &#x201c;Other&#x201d; line on our consolidated statement of cash flows.  After construction of the Gray Oak Pipeline is fully completed, these restrictions expire, and the sale will be recognized under GAAP.  Phillips 66 Partners will continue to control and consolidate Holdings LLC after sale recognition, and therefore the third party&#x2019;s &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;35%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; interest will be recharacterized from a long-term obligation to a noncontrolling interest on our consolidated balance sheet at that time.  Also at that time, the premium paid will be recharacterized from a long-term obligation to a gain in our consolidated statement of income.  For the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;six months ended&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June&#160;30, 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, the third party contributed an aggregate of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$341 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; into Holdings LLC, which Holdings LLC used to fund its portion of Gray Oak&#x2019;s cash calls. <th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Changes in Accounting Principles<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">6 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Jun. 30, 2019</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AccountingChangesAndErrorCorrectionsAbstract', window );"><strong>Accounting Changes and Error Corrections [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AccountingChangesTextBlock', window );">Changes in Accounting Principles</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 2&#8212;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Accounting Principles</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"> </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, we elected to adopt Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No. 2018-02, &#8220;Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic 220): Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income.&#8221;  This ASU permits the deferred income tax effects stranded in accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) resulting from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the Tax Act) enacted in December 2017 to be reclassified to retained earnings.  As of January 1, 2019, we recorded a cumulative effect adjustment to our opening consolidated balance sheet to reclassify an aggregate income tax benefit of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$89 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, primarily related to our pension plans, from accumulated other comprehensive loss to retained earnings. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, we early adopted ASU 2016-13, &#8220;Financial Instruments&#8212;Credit Losses (Topic 326):  Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments,&#8221; using the modified retrospective transition method.  This ASU amends the impairment model to utilize an expected loss methodology in place of the incurred loss methodology for financial instruments, including trade receivables, and off-balance sheet credit exposures.  The amendment requires entities to consider a broader range of information to estimate expected credit losses, which may result in earlier recognition of losses.  We recorded a noncash cumulative effect adjustment to retained earnings of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$9 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, net of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$3 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> of income taxes, on our opening consolidated balance sheet as of January 1, 2019.  See </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 4&#8212;Credit Losses</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for more information on our presentation of credit losses.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, we adopted ASU No. 2016-02, &#8220;Leases (Topic 842),&#8221; using the modified retrospective transition method.  The new standard establishes a right-of-use (ROU) model that requires a lessee to record a ROU asset and a lease liability on the consolidated balance sheet for all leases with terms longer than 12 months.  Leases will continue to be classified as either finance or operating, with classification affecting the pattern of expense recognition in the consolidated income statement.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We elected the package of practical expedients that allowed us to carry forward our determination of whether an arrangement contained a lease and lease classification, as well as our accounting for initial direct costs for existing contracts.  We recorded a noncash cumulative effect adjustment to our opening consolidated balance sheet as of January 1, 2019, to record an aggregate operating lease ROU asset and corresponding lease liability of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$1,415 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and immaterial adjustments to retained earnings and noncontrolling interests.  See </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 14&#8212;Leases</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for the new lease disclosures required by this ASU.</span></div><span></span>
</td>

See Note 12&#8212;Derivatives and Financial Instruments, for additional information.</span></div></td></tr><tr><td colspan="11" style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;">** Sales and other operating revenues are attributable to countries based on the location of the operations generating the revenues.</span></div><div style="text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div></td></tr></table></div><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Contract-Related Assets and Liabilities</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, receivables from contracts with customers were </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$5,385 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$4,993 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, respectively.  Significant non-customer balances, such as buy/sell receivables and excise tax receivables, were excluded from these amounts. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Our contract-related assets also include payments we make to our marketing customers related to incentive programs.  An incentive payment is initially recognized as an asset and subsequently amortized as a reduction to revenue over the contract term, which generally ranges from </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>5</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>15</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> years.  At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, our asset balances related to such payments were </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$287 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$248 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, respectively. </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Our contract liabilities represent advances from our customers prior to product or service delivery.  At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, contract liabilities were </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$77 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$99 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, respectively.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Remaining Performance Obligations</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Most of our contracts with customers are spot contracts or term contracts with only variable consideration.  We do not disclose remaining performance obligations for these contracts as the expected duration is one year or less or because the variable consideration has been allocated entirely to an unsatisfied performance obligation.  We also have certain contracts in our Midstream segment that include minimum volume commitments with fixed pricing, most of which expire by 2021.  At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, the remaining performance obligations related to these minimum volume commitment contracts were not material.</span></div><span></span>

<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 4&#8212;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Credit Losses</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">&#160;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We are exposed to credit losses primarily through our sales of refined petroleum products, crude oil and NGLs.  We assess each counterparty&#8217;s ability to pay for the products we sell by conducting a credit review.  The credit review considers our expected billing exposure and timing for payment and the counterparty&#8217;s established credit rating or our assessment of the counterparty&#8217;s creditworthiness based on our analysis of their financial statements when a credit rating is not available.  We also consider contract terms and conditions, country and political risk, and business strategy in our evaluation.  A credit limit is established for each counterparty based on the outcome of this review.  We may require collateralized asset support or a prepayment to mitigate credit risk.  </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We monitor our ongoing credit exposure through active review of counterparty balances against contract terms and due dates.  Our activities include timely account reconciliation, dispute resolution and payment confirmation.  We may employ collection agencies and legal counsel to pursue recovery of defaulted receivables.  </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, we reported </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$6,727 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> of accounts and notes receivable, net of allowances of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$41 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Changes in the allowance were not material for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">three and six months</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Based on an aging analysis at </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>99%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> of our accounts receivable were outstanding less than 60 days, with the remainder outstanding less than 90 days.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We are also exposed to credit losses from off-balance sheet exposures, such as guarantees of joint venture debt, residual value guarantees of leased assets and standby letters of credit. style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">DCP Midstream, LLC (DCP Midstream)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">The fair value of our investment in DCP Midstream depends on the market value of DCP Midstream&#8217;s general partner interest in its master limited partnership (MLP), DCP Midstream, LP (DCP Partners) and the market value of DCP Partners&#8217; common units.  Recent declines in DCP Partners&#8217; common unit price and MLP valuations have negatively impacted the fair value of our investment in DCP Midstream.  At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, we estimated the fair value of our investment in DCP Midstream was approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>10%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> below our current book value of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$2.3 billion</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  We currently believe this condition is temporary.  However, we may subsequently conclude the reduction in fair value is other-than-temporary and impair our investment in DCP Midstream if market conditions do not sustainably improve in the near future.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">Dakota Access, LLC (Dakota Access) and Energy Transfer Crude Oil Company, LLC (ETCO)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">In March 2019, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dakota Access closed an offering of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$2,500 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> aggregate principal amount of unsecured senior notes.  The net proceeds from the issuance of these notes were used to repay amounts outstanding under existing credit facilities of Dakota Access and ETCO.  Dakota Access and ETCO have guaranteed repayment of the notes.  In addition, Phillips 66 Partners LP (Phillips 66 Partners) and its co-venturers in Dakota Access provided a Contingent Equity Contribution Undertaking (CECU) in conjunction with the notes offering.  Under the CECU, if Dakota Access receives an unfavorable court ruling related to certain disputed construction permits and Dakota Access determines that an equity contribution trigger event has occurred, the venturers may be severally required to make proportionate equity contributions to Dakota Access and ETCO up to an aggregate maximum of approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$2,525 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; share of the maximum potential equity contributions under the CECU is approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$631 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">Gray Oak Pipeline, LLC (Gray Oak)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">In February 2019, Gray Oak Holdings LLC (Holdings LLC), a consolidated subsidiary of Phillips 66 Partners, transferred a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>10%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> ownership interest in Gray Oak to a third party that exercised a purchase option, for proceeds of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$81 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  This transfer was accounted for as a sale and resulted in a decrease in Holdings LLC&#8217;s ownership interest in Gray Oak from </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>75%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>65%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and the recognition of an immaterial gain.  The proceeds received from this sale are presented as an investing cash inflow in the &#8220;Proceeds from asset dispositions&#8221; line on our consolidated statement of cash flows. At  </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; effective ownership interest in the Gray Oak Pipeline was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>42.25%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Phillips 66 Partners accounts for the investment in Gray Oak under the equity method because it does not have sufficient voting rights over key governance provisions to assert control over Gray Oak.  Gray Oak is considered a variable interest entity (VIE) because it does not have sufficient equity at risk to fully fund the construction of all assets required for principal operations.  Phillips 66 Partners has determined it is not the primary beneficiary because it and its co-venturers jointly direct the activities of Gray Oak that most significantly impact economic performance.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">In </span><span style="font-size:10.5pt;">June 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Gray Oak entered into a third-party term loan facility with an initial borrowing capacity of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$1,230 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, which was increased in </span><span style="font-size:10.5pt;">July 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$1,317 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Borrowings under the facility are due on </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;3, 2022</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Phillips 66 Partners and its co-venturers provided a guarantee through an equity contribution agreement requiring proportionate equity contributions to Gray Oak up to the total outstanding loan amount.  Under the agreement, Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; maximum potential amount of future obligations is </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$556 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, plus any accrued interest and associated fees, which would be required if the term loan facility is fully utilized and Gray Oak defaults on its obligations.  At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Gray Oak had borrowings of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$551 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> outstanding, and Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>42.25%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> proportionate exposure under the equity contribution agreement was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$233 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  The net proceeds from the term loan were used by Gray Oak for construction of the Gray Oak Pipeline and repayment of amounts borrowed under a related party loan agreement that Phillips 66 Partners and its co-venturers executed in </span><span style="font-size:10.5pt;">March 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and terminated upon the repayment by Gray Oak in </span><span style="font-size:10.5pt;">June</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  The total related party loan to and repayment received from Gray Oak was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$95 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> during the second quarter of 2019.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; maximum exposure to loss was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$978 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, which represented the book value of the investment in Gray Oak of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$745 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and the term loan guarantee of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$233 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  See </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 21&#8212;Phillips 66 Partners LP</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for additional information regarding Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; ownership in Holdings LLC and Gray Oak.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">OnCue Holdings, LLC (OnCue)</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We hold a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>50%</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> interest in OnCue, a joint venture that owns and operates retail convenience stores.  We fully guaranteed various debt agreements of OnCue and our co-venturer did not participate in the guarantees.  This entity is considered a VIE because our debt guarantees resulted in OnCue not being exposed to all potential losses.  We have determined we are not the primary beneficiary because we do not have the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact economic performance.  At </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">June&#160;30, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, our maximum exposure to loss was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$131 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, which represented the book value of our investment in OnCue of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$72 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and guaranteed debt obligations of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><span>$59 million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</span></div><span></span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for equity method investments and joint ventures. Equity method investments are investments that give the investor the ability to exercise significant influence over the operating and financial policies of an investee. Joint ventures are entities owned and operated by a small group of businesses as a separate and specific business or project for the mutual benefit of the members of the group.</p></div>

<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_EarningsPerShareTextBlock', window );">Earnings Per Share</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;color:#000000;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;">Note 8&#8212;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;color:#000000;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;">Earnings Per Share</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"> </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">The numerator of basic earnings per share (EPS) is net income attributable to Phillips 66, reduced by noncancelable dividends paid on unvested share-based employee awards during the vesting period (participating securities).  The denominator of basic EPS is the sum of the daily weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the periods presented and fully vested stock and unit awards that have not yet been issued as common stock.  The numerator of diluted EPS is also based on net income attributable to Phillips 66, which is reduced only by dividend equivalents paid on participating securities for which the dividends are more dilutive than the participation of the awards in the earnings of the periods presented.  To the extent unvested stock, unit or option awards and vested unexercised stock options are dilutive, they are included with the weighted-average common shares outstanding in the denominator.  Treasury stock is excluded from the denominator in both basic and diluted EPS.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> <a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for information about short-term and long-term debt arrangements, which includes amounts of borrowings under each line of credit, note payable, commercial paper issue, bonds indenture, debenture issue, own-share lending arrangements and any other contractual agreement to repay funds, and about the underlying arrangements, rationale for a classification as long-term, including repayment terms, interest rates, collateral provided, restrictions on use of assets and activities, whether or not in compliance with debt covenants, and other matters important to users of the financial statements, such as the effects of refinancing and noncompliance with debt covenants.</p></div>

<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_GuaranteesAbstract', window );"><strong>Guarantees [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
